profiles.meeting_scenario: At an asset management firm, a design review is being held for a proposal to adapt an academic-style AI trading strategy for the firm's internal research pipeline. The proposal combines a Hidden Markov Model with a neural network and feeds the resulting signals into a Black-Litterman portfolio construction layer for a U.S. energy equities sleeve. The review is focused on whether the current design is ready to move from research replication into the firm's controlled paper-trading environment. The agenda is to assess the proposed system architecture, the backtest replication approach on QuantConnect, operational readiness of the training and warm-up setup, and whether the risk and execution assumptions are sufficiently covered for an internal go-ahead. The expected outcome is a conditional approval with a list of revisions before implementation begins.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Statistical arbitrage, regime models, portfolio construction, research reproducibility
members.background: Elena leads the firm's cross-asset quant research pod and previously worked at a systematic hedge fund building market regime and allocation models for equities and commodities.
members.private_state: She wants the design approved as a faithful and efficient internal replication of the published approach, while quietly avoiding scope creep that would delay her team's quarterly research commitments.
hidden_assumptions: A design being 'ready for paper trading' means the research logic is reproducible and stable enough to run end-to-end in the firm's sandbox, even if some production controls are still placeholders.

The stated 'three-year warm-up' is naturally understood as a one-time historical data buffer used to initialize both the HMM state estimation and the neural network features before the first live decision date.

Reviewing 'risk management' in this meeting means checking whether the two modeled risk layers and the Black-Litterman constraints are conceptually integrated into the strategy design, not validating downstream desk limits or compliance overlays.
The 'COVID period results' refers to the 2019-2022 evaluation window reported in the paper and used for replication benchmarking.
Replication on QuantConnect implies using its standard adjusted historical data and event-driven backtest flow unless a deviation is called out explicitly.

members.name: Marcus Bell
members.expertise: Research platform onboarding, trading system controls, model deployment, portfolio implementation
members.background: Marcus manages the team that turns approved quant research into governed paper-trading and pre-production workflows, with prior experience in execution engineering for long-short equity strategies.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid approving a design that later creates onboarding friction for his team, so he is listening for signs that the strategy can be slotted into existing paper-trading controls without hidden rework.
hidden_assumptions: A design being 'ready for paper trading' means it already fits the operational conventions used by the onboarding team, including recurring retraining schedules, monitoring hooks, and clearly bounded implementation dependencies.

The stated 'three-year warm-up' is naturally interpreted as a rolling lookback that the algorithm continues to maintain for periodic retraining and state refresh during paper trading, not merely an initial bootstrap window.

Reviewing 'risk management' in this meeting includes all protections that would materially shape paper-trading behavior, including liquidity caps, broker-cost handling, position throttles, and desk-level guardrails.
The 'COVID period results' is shorthand for the stressed market regime demonstrated during the 2020-2022 disruption period, which is the relevant benchmark for evaluating robustness claims.

Replication on QuantConnect still requires explicit confirmation of data conventions because paper-trading onboarding usually mirrors the firm's own adjusted-price and rebalance scheduling standards rather than assuming platform defaults.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'ready for paper trading'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design should be 'ready for paper trading' after this review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the research design is sufficiently replicated, stable, and documented to run as an internal experiment in a sandbox, with some operational details to be filled in later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the design should already satisfy the practical onboarding criteria his team uses before they allocate engineering time, including retraining cadence, monitoring expectations, and integration boundaries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In firms with staged model governance, 'paper trading' is a familiar milestone term that sounds shared; each person assumes the other is using the organization's obvious definition, so neither pauses to unpack the threshold.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to preserving the paper's 'three-year warm-up' in the design.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means a one-time initialization window before the strategy starts producing signals, used to seed model state and feature history.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the system should continuously maintain a three-year rolling window that supports periodic retraining and state refreshes during paper trading.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A warm-up period is standard vocabulary in backtesting and deployment discussions, and both interpretations sound operationally sensible; because they agree the same number and phrase should stay in place, the implementation gap remains invisible.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of 'risk management' in the review
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the design already includes 'two risk models and risk management.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the strategy's internal risk modeling and portfolio construction logic, specifically the two modeled risk layers and Black-Litterman optimization constraints described in the proposal.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the full set of risk-related controls that will affect behavior in paper trading, including execution cost treatment, liquidity throttles, concentration caps, and implementation guardrails in addition to the modeling layer.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The proposal itself uses broad risk language, so each person comfortably maps the phrase onto their own domain; since both are discussing legitimate forms of risk management, their surface agreement feels complete rather than ambiguous.

misalignment_points.topic: Which period the 'COVID results' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both cite the strategy's 'COVID period results' as the benchmark for replication quality.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the full 2019-2022 backtest window cited in the study, including pre-shock, shock, and recovery phases.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is thinking mainly of the stressed 2020-2022 span, when volatility and operational stress would be most informative for onboarding confidence.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The label 'COVID period' is commonly used loosely, and both windows are plausible interpretations of the same phrase; because neither person's comments directly conflict, the mismatch persists beneath apparent agreement.
